Group Risk Management Policy GRP-POL-001 | Version 6.0 | Internal

Cadence Financial Group, Inc. (the "“Group") accepts risk as an inherent consequence of providing investment banking, asset
management and consumer banking services. This policy establishes the Group-wide framework through which risk is identified,
assessed, treated, monitored and reported, so that risk-taking is deliberate, understood, and remains within the appetite set by the
Board of Directors.

This policy is the apex document of the Group risk policy hierarchy. All subordinate risk policies, standards and procedures must be
consistent with it. Where a subordinate document conflicts with this policy, this policy prevails. Interpretation questions are directed to
the policy author, [PERSON_NAME: Tobias Lindqvist] ([EMAIL: t.lindqvist@cadencefg.com], [PHONE: +44 20 7555 0171]).

1. Protect capital, liquidity and earnings by ensuring exposures remain within approved appetite and regulatory limits.
2. Enable informed risk-taking through a consistent, comparable view of risk across business lines and geographies.
3. Establish clear accountability for every material risk, with a single named owner at an appropriate level of seniority.
4. Ensure regulatory compliance with prudential, conduct and data-protection obligations in each jurisdiction.
5. Protect customers and market integrity by embedding conduct considerations into risk decisions.
6. Safeguard reputation by identifying and managing risks to stakeholder confidence.

7. Support resilience so the Group can absorb severe but plausible shocks and continue important business services.
8. Promote a healthy risk culture in which concerns are raised early, escalated without fear, and acted upon.

children.text: Risk is owned by the business that creates it. Ownership cannot be delegated to a control function or to a third party.
The depth of assessment, control and reporting is proportionate to the materiality and complexity of the risk.
The second and third lines have direct, unrestricted access to the Board and are free from business pressure.
Risks are reported completely and without filtering. Understating or delaying a risk report is a breach of this policy.
The framework considers emerging and prospective risks, not only realised losses and historical events.
Acommon taxonomy, scoring scale and definitions apply Group-wide so that risks aggregate meaningfully.
Assessments reflect actual exposure and actual control operation, not documented intent.

Each principal supervisory relationship has a single named owner accountable for the accuracy and timeliness of submissions and for
coordinating examination responses.
3.3 Relationship to the internal control framework

Risk assessment determines what could go wrong and how severely; the control framework determines what is done to prevent or
detect it. The two are linked through the control library, in which every control maps to at least one risk in the Group Risk Register, and
every risk rated Elevated or above maps to at least one control.
3.4 Relationship to capital and liquidity planning

The output of risk identification and assessment is a direct input to the Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Process (ICAAP) and the
Internal Liquidity Adequacy Assessment Process (ILAAP). Material risks not adequately captured by regulatory capital requirements are
assessed for Pillar 2 add-ons by the Group Treasurer, [PERSON_NAME: Marta Szewczyk] ([EMAIL: m.szewczyk@cadencefg.com]), with challenge from the Group
Chief Risk Officer.

Each regulated subsidiary maintains a board-approved local addendum documenting the local regulatory overlay, the composition of the
local risk committee and the delegated authorities of local management. Local addenda may narrow Group appetite but may never
widen it. Cross-border data flows arising from Group-level risk aggregation — which include the employee identifiers and contact details
reproduced throughout this policy — are assessed under the Data Privacy Policy before transfer.

The first line comprises revenue-generating businesses and the operational and support functions that execute transactions and
processes. It owns its risks outright, designs and operates controls, performs RCSA, self-identifies issues, records incidents and
remains accountable for remediation to completion. Accountability is not transferred by the existence of second-line oversight or third-
line assurance.

The second line comprises the Group Risk function, Compliance and the Data Privacy Office. It sets the framework, taxonomy,
methodology and policy; defines appetite metrics and tolerances; provides independent, evidenced challenge to first-line assessments;
aggregates and reports the Group risk profile; and approves exceptions and acceptances within delegated authority. Where a second-
line function operates a control of its own — for example sanctions screening, operated by [PERSON_NAME: Fumiko L. Nakagawa]'s team — it is a first-
line activity for that control and is subject to independent challenge accordingly.

Group Internal Audit provides independent assurance to the Board on governance, risk management and internal control. It has
unrestricted access to all records, systems, personnel and premises. It does not design controls, make management decisions or own
risk. The Chief Internal Auditor, [PERSON_NAME: Ifeoma C. Adeyemi] ([EMPLOYEE_ID: EMP-41455], [EMAIL: i.adeyemi@cadencefg.com]), reports functionally to the Chair of the
Audit Committee and administratively to the Chief Executive; her appointment, removal and remuneration are matters reserved to the
Audit Committee.

Risk appetite is the aggregate level and type of risk the Group is willing to assume in pursuit of its strategy. It is the primary mechanism
by which the Board constrains executive risk-taking, and it is expressed so that it can be measured, monitored and breached observably.

children.text:
The maximum risk the Group could absorb before viability is threatened, bounded by
capital, liquidity and regulatory minima.

The level of risk the Group chooses to accept, set materially inside capacity to
preserve a management buffer.

Permissible variation around each appetite measure; breaching tolerance triggers
escalation but is not itself a policy breach.

Hard boundaries cascaded to divisions, desks, portfolios and counterparties. A limit
breach is a policy breach.
Early-warning thresholds set inside limits, prompting action before a limit is reached.

blocks.text:
Appetite is reviewed at least annually, in parallel with the strategic and financial planning cycle, so that the plan and the appetite
constraining it are agreed together rather than sequentially. The Group CRO recommends the statement, drawing on the risk profile,
capital and liquidity position, stress testing results and the emerging risk scan. Out-of-cycle review is triggered by a material acquisition
or disposal, a material regulatory change, a Critical-rated incident, or any breach of a Board-level appetite measure.

Prohibited practice. Limits must not be amended to cure an existing breach. Any limit change proposed within thirty days of a breach
of that limit requires explicit Board Risk Committee approval, and the Committee must be provided with the breach history alongside the
proposal.

Group appetite is cascaded to divisions, and from divisions to business units, desks and portfolios. The sum of cascaded limits may be
less than the Group limit but may never exceed it. Divisional limits are approved by the Group Executive Risk Committee and reviewed
whenever Group appetite changes. Each business unit head must demonstrate the line of sight from local limits to the Board-approved
statement.

Adherence to appetite is a mandatory input to performance assessment for all material risk takers. The Remuneration Committee
receives an annual risk conduct report from the Group CRO covering appetite breaches, unremediated overdue issues, Critical incidents
and audit findings attributable to each named individual. The Committee may apply in-year adjustment, malus or clawback where risk
outcomes warrant it. A favourable financial result achieved outside appetite is not a basis for reward.

Where an event could fall into more than one category it is classified by root cause, not by the form of the consequence. A customer
refund arising from a system defect is operational risk (technology), not conduct risk, although the conduct consequence is recorded
alongside it. Where a single event has consequences in several categories, the primary classification is used for aggregation and
secondary tags are applied for analysis.

The Group applies a single, continuous process to every risk category. The depth of application is proportionate to materiality, but no
step may be omitted.

Each identified risk is assessed on an inherent basis and then residually, using the scales at Appendix A. Assessment is evidence-
based: a residual rating may be reduced below inherent only where relevant controls have been assessed as both appropriately
designed and operating effectively, with evidence retained. The residual rating is then compared against appetite. Where residual risk
exceeds appetite the risk must be treated, not merely recorded. Where residual risk is materially below appetite, the business should
consider whether controls are disproportionate; over-control is a legitimate finding.

Monitoring combines key risk indicators, control testing, thematic reviews and independent assurance, proportionate to the residual
rating as set out in Section 14.3. Reporting is a step in the process, not an administrative by-product: a risk identified and assessed but
not reported through the correct forum has not been managed.

Communication takes place throughout the process rather than only at its conclusion. Risk owners must consult affected functions —
including Legal (R. [PERSON_NAME: M. Achterberg]), Compliance ([PERSON_NAME: F. L. Nakagawa]), Finance ([PERSON_NAME: Y. A. Sorokina]), Technology ([PERSON_NAME: C. A. Whitfield]) and the Data
Privacy Office ([PERSON_NAME: H. Vorstermann]) — before finalising assessments and treatment plans touching their domains.

Risk is scored as the product of impact and likelihood, each rated on a five-point scale, producing a score between 1 and 25 which maps
to one of five bands. The same scale applies to inherent and residual assessments and to every risk category, so that a High rating

means the same thing in credit risk as in technology risk.

17. Emerging risk, scenario analysis and stress testing

Emerging risks are newly developing or changing risks whose impact and likelihood cannot yet be reliably quantified. Because they are
by definition absent from historical loss data, they will not be surfaced by backward-looking processes and require deliberate horizon
scanning.

The Group Risk function performs a quarterly emerging risk scan drawing on regulatory pipelines, supervisory publications, industry
bodies, peer loss events, technology developments, macroeconomic and geopolitical analysis, climate science and input from the
business. Candidate risks are assessed for velocity as well as potential impact and presented to the Group Executive Risk Committee
with a recommended treatment: monitor, investigate, or escalate to the register.

Scenario analysis assesses exposure to severe but plausible events for which historical data is unavailable or unrepresentative.
Scenarios are developed through facilitated workshops with business, risk and subject-matter experts, and must explicitly record
assumptions made, the control environment assumed, estimated frequency and severity, and the range of uncertainty around the
estimate.

Stress testing quantifies the effect of adverse conditions on capital, liquidity and earnings. The Group conducts regulatory prescribed
tests, internal tests aligned to its own profile, and reverse stress tests identifying circumstances under which the business model would
become unviable. Reverse stress testing results are reported to the Board annually and inform the Recovery Plan. Assumptions and the
sensitivity of results to them are disclosed alongside results; a stress result presented without its assumptions is not a valid report.

The Group identifies its important business services, maps the people, processes, technology, facilities, data and third parties on which
each depends, and sets a Board-approved impact tolerance for each. It then tests its ability to remain within those tolerances under
severe but plausible disruption. Where testing shows a tolerance cannot be met, the gap is recorded as an issue and remediated under
Section 15.

Scenario and stress results are not standalone exercises. They must demonstrably inform capital and liquidity planning, appetite
calibration, the Recovery Plan, resilience investment and the risk register. The Group Executive Risk Committee reviews the use made
of each exercise and reports to the Board Risk Committee where results have not been acted upon.

18. Change, new product and third-party risk

Change is a significant source of operational risk. All material change initiatives — system implementations, migrations, organisational
restructures, outsourcing transitions and regulatory implementation programmes — require a risk assessment at initiation, at each major
stage gate and prior to go-live. The assessment must address risks introduced by the change, risks to business-as-usual during
transition, control coverage during parallel running, and the rollback position if the change fails.

Go-live approval requires confirmation that controls have been designed, implemented and tested; that data migration has been
reconciled; that affected staff have been trained; that support arrangements are in place; and that a documented rollback plan exists.
Go-live may not proceed on the basis that controls will be implemented shortly afterwards.

No new product, service, market or distribution channel may be launched without approval from the New Product Approval Committee,
chaired by [PERSON_NAME: Priyanka S. Raghavan]. A material change to an existing product requires the same approval. The submission must address,
at minimum: target market, customer need and foreseeable harm; risk assessment across every applicable taxonomy category; legal,
regulatory, tax and accounting analysis; financial crime, sanctions and conduct assessment; a data privacy impact assessment where
personal data is processed; technology, resilience and third-party dependencies; operational readiness; pricing, profitability and capital
consumption; and exit and wind-down arrangements.

Every approved product is subject to post-implementation review within twelve months, assessing whether the product performed as
expected, whether customer outcomes matched those anticipated, and whether the risk assessment remains valid.

Third-party arrangements are managed across the full lifecycle: strategy and sourcing, due diligence, contracting, onboarding, ongoing
monitoring and exit. Depth of oversight is determined by criticality tier, assessed on the importance of the service, the sensitivity of data
shared, the substitutability of the provider and the regulatory classification of the arrangement.

blocks.text:
All exceptions are recorded in the Group Exception Register maintained by the Group Risk function. The register is reported to the
Group Executive Risk Committee monthly and to the Board Risk Committee quarterly, including total count, ageing profile, exceptions
extended more than once, and any that have expired without remediation. Operating under an expired exception is a policy breach.

No exception is available from a legal or regulatory requirement, from a zero-appetite statement, or from the incident reporting
obligation in Section 16.1. Where compliance with a legal requirement is not achievable, the matter is escalated immediately to the
Group General Counsel ([PERSON_NAME: R. M. Achterberg], [EMAIL: r.achterberg@cadencefg.com]) and the Board Risk Committee.

Group Internal Audit reviews the design and operating effectiveness of the enterprise risk management framework at least once every
two years and reports its opinion to the Audit Committee and the Board Risk Committee. The Group CRO additionally presents an
annual framework effectiveness review to the Board covering governance, appetite, process, data, systems, resourcing and culture,
stating explicitly any areas where the framework is not yet operating as intended.

Completion of mandatory training is a Board-level appetite measure with a target of at least 95 per cent. Non-completion is escalated to
the relevant divisional CEO and is an input to performance assessment.

Risk culture comprises the shared norms and behaviours determining how risk is actually treated, as distinct from how policy states it
should be. The Group assesses its culture annually using employee survey results, Speak Up volumes and themes, incident and issue
self-identification rates, RCSA challenge outcomes, exception and acceptance volumes, and behavioural indicators drawn from
performance and conduct data.

A high proportion of issues identified by the business itself, rather than by audit or regulators, is treated as a positive indicator. A low
incident reporting volume is investigated rather than celebrated, on the basis that it more often indicates under-reporting than an
absence of incidents.

All individuals may raise concerns confidentially, and anonymously where they choose, through the Group Speak Up channel operated
independently of line management. Concerns relating to risk, control, conduct or compliance are routed to the appropriate function for
investigation, with oversight by the Audit Committee. Retaliation against any person raising a concern in good faith is a serious
disciplinary matter, whether or not the concern is ultimately substantiated.

current, ensuring subordinate documents remain aligned, and reporting on its effectiveness to the Board Risk Committee.

The policy is reviewed at least annually. Out-of-cycle review is triggered by a material change to strategy, structure or business model; a
material change to applicable regulation; a Critical-rated incident or material regulatory finding relating to risk management; a material
change to the appetite statement; or a recommendation from Group Internal Audit or the Board Risk Committee.

Material amendments require Board Risk Committee approval. Non-material amendments — typographical corrections, role title
updates, references and formatting — may be approved by the Group CRO and are reported to the Board Risk Committee at its next
meeting. Where there is doubt, the amendment is treated as material.

Failure to comply with this policy is a breach and may constitute misconduct. Breaches are recorded as incidents under Section 16 and
investigated proportionately. The following are treated as serious breaches and reported to the Board Risk Committee individually:
¢ Failure to report a known incident, near miss or loss event.
* Knowingly false or misleading attestation, assessment or report.
* Operating outside an approved limit without escalation.
* Operating under an expired risk acceptance or exception.
¢« Amending a limit or a rating to conceal or cure a breach.
* Retaliation against an individual who has raised a concern in good faith.
* Obstructing the second or third line in the performance of their duties.

Confirmed breaches are referred to Human Resources (D. [PERSON_NAME: R. Okonjo], [EMAIL: d.okonjo@cadencefg.com]) for consideration under the
disciplinary process and, for material risk takers, reported to the Remuneration Committee for consideration of variable-pay adjustment.
